what: Michael D. Kelly's Stanford AI Project thesis (AIM-130) described a program that picked out, from TV-camera pictures of people, those showing the same person, using automatically extracted head outlines and body/face measurements.
fit: A computer, working from TV-camera images with no human marking of features, matched people's pictures against a collection of stored pictures to decide which depicted the same person.

sources.title: Project Technical Report (A.I. Memo abstracts, incl. AIM-130 Visual Identification of People by Computer)
sources.quote: pictures of people taken by a TV camera, those pictures that depict the same person

sources.title: Facial recognition system
sources.quote: In 1970, Takeo Kanade publicly demonstrated a face-matching system that located anatomical features

note: Second pass chose Kanade 1970 (Wikipedia). Kelly's July 1970 Stanford thesis is a contemporary, fully computer-based face-matching system of the same year, so the year is unchanged but the source is now contemporary. Earlier candidate: Bledsoe, Chan and Bisson / Panoramic Research 'man-machine' face recognition (proposal Jan 1963, work 1964-66): the computer matched stored feature distances, but a human had to locate features on photographs by tablet, no camera, so rejected as not automated. Kanade's own thesis is 1973, later. Month is the thesis month; the Jan 1970 AIM-108 head-outline paper is its precursor.
searched: archive.org full-text (ia_search3) for 'face recognition' 1960-75, 'Bledsoe facial recognition' 1960-75, 'Visual identification of people by computer' 1969-73; page_text3 on DTIC AD0724867 and AD0776233; Wikipedia Facial recognition system. DTIC AD0713252 (the thesis itself) has no OCR text; Google Books unavailable.

what: By 1994 facial-recognition biometric products had reached the marketplace (access control); the DMV offices of West Virginia and New Mexico followed, using automated face recognition against duplicate licences after the 1993 FERET test.
fit: Commercial systems used cameras and computers to match a person's face against an enrolled stored image for entry control and identity checks.

sources.title: Biometric Identification Verification Technology Status and Feasibility Study
sources.quote: Systems which have reached the marketplace include fingerprint, thumbprint, hand geometry, keystroke dynamics, signature dynamics, voice patterns, retina patterns, and facial recognition.

sources.title: Facial recognition system
sources.quote: became the first DMV offices to use automated facial recognition systems to prevent people from obtaining multiple driving licenses

note: Replaces second pass 1997 (ZN-Face sale). The 1994 DTIC study says facial recognition products were already on the market but names no deployment and calls them unreliable (it judged them unable to meet DoD needs), so the date is the earliest documented market presence, not a documented first user. The DMV use (West Virginia, New Mexico) is after 1993 but I found no dated source. Mexico 2000 and Super Bowl 2001 are later.
searched: ia_search3 'face recognition' driver license 1993-99, Viisage / Visionics / Miros 1994-99, 'facial recognition' police/casino 1990-96; Wikipedia Facial recognition system; websearch for first DMV use (no dated source). SPIE 1996 law-enforcement proceedings and Encyclopedia of Emerging Industries not readable (lending, 401).

what: Apple announced Face ID on the iPhone X (September 2017), putting face recognition unlock on a mass-market phone.
fit: A camera and processor match the user's face against a stored face model to unlock the phone and authorise purchases.

sources.title: Face ID
sources.quote: Apple announced Face ID alongside the iPhone X on September 12, 2017

note: Kept from second pass. Earlier consumer face matching existed: Android 4.0 Face Unlock (2011), photo-tagging suggestions in consumer photo software and social networks (c.2009-2010), but I could not fetch dated sources for them; Face ID is the date of introduction, not a measured adoption figure.
searched: Wikipedia Face ID; Apple newsroom page timed out; no usage-share source found.

concept_note: First demonstration kept at 1970 but re-sourced to Kelly's contemporary Stanford thesis (Kanade's system is a Wikipedia claim); first practical use moved earlier from 1997 to 1994 on a contemporary DTIC study (low confidence); mass adoption unchanged (2017).
